artifacts.title: Review Prep — Kegl, 21 Sep
artifacts.desc: Prep for the contract re-appointment review with Rosemary Kegl (English Dept executive). Built on the signed offer letter of 2 June 2025, which had sat unread in the workspace for fifteen months: Senior Lecturer, 1 July 2025 through 30 June 2028, $65,000 earned across a 10-month period and re-set every spring, a $2,000/yr professional development fund with $4,000 carryover, and the entire production operation assigned as formal terms of the appointment. The lead is a governance gap, not a salary number: Senior Lecturer is TEACHING track, and the University's reappointment machinery in Appendix II Section II is written for the INSTRUCTIONAL ranks, so no procedure in either Appendix II or the Jan 2025 Faculty Handbook covers this review. Three gaps documented by section number - no process, no notification guarantee (Handbook IV.A.1 omits lecturer and senior lecturer), and a definition that only appears under Part-Time titles. The leverage sits inside the letter itself: policy says teaching-track faculty are hired to teach without expectation of other service, while the letter assigns the whole operation. Conversion to Associate Professor of Instruction skips assistant entirely and is administrative, but carries no automatic raise, which is what the market data is for: 52 live postings, academic production at a $67,388 median against $106,250 regional, his $65,000 below his own sector's floor and understated further because it is a 10-month figure. Nine external comps with payroll records held strictly separate from offer bands, Yale's 10-month TD row flagged as the only true apples-to-apples. Five asks in priority order with Handbook citations, Milo's verified six production units against the four the program advertises, and a what-this-does-not-know block led by the unknown current salary. Phone-first: no wide tables, stacked rows throughout.
